clauses.title: Payment intent idempotency
clauses.summary: POST /v1/payment_intents MUST accept an Idempotency-Key header; duplicate keys MUST NOT create a second intent and MUST return the original intent resource.

clauses.title: Webhook signature verification
clauses.summary: Every inbound Stripe webhook MUST be verified against the Stripe-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256, timestamp tolerance) before any business logic; failed/missing signatures MUST be rejected with HTTP 400 and MUST NOT trigger payment side effects.

clauses.title: Refund cap
clauses.summary: A refund MUST NOT exceed the total captured amount; cumulative refunds against one payment MUST NOT exceed captured; over-cap attempts MUST be rejected and MUST NOT create a negative or over-refunded balance.

clauses.title: Ledger available-vs-pending
clauses.summary: GET /v1/ledger/balances MUST report distinct 'available' and 'pending' figures; held funds MUST be reported under pending and MUST NOT be included in available or be spendable.

clauses.title: Token type interchange
clauses.summary: The implementation MUST distinguish JWT access tokens from raw API keys at validation time; a JWT to an API-key endpoint and an API key to a JWT endpoint MUST both be rejected, with no fallback treating either as the other.

clauses.title: Retry & circuit-breaker discipline
clauses.summary: Outbound calls receiving 429 or 5xx SHALL retry with exponential backoff plus jitter; the circuit breaker SHALL NOT trip on the first transient error, SHALL require the consecutive-failure threshold, and SHALL NOT open half-open earlier than the runbook settle window.

clauses.title: Monetary precision in integer cents
clauses.summary: All currency arithmetic MUST be performed in integer cents; floats MUST NOT be used for money; decimal-string inputs MUST be parsed to exact integer cents (round-half-even) and stored as integers.

clauses.title: Async worker resilience / no null-deref outage
clauses.summary: The async billing processor MUST nil-guard the Stripe customer record before dereference; a missing/unparseable record MUST be isolated to that item (not crash the whole batch); per-item failures MUST be recorded while remaining items still process.
